local_entities.label: Voyager branch A after spatial scission
Voyager branch B after spatial scission
Harry Kim transferred from surviving/destroyed-ship counterpart branch
Wildman infant transferred from intact branch

evidence.summary: After subspace turbulence, one Voyager experiences severe damage and unexplained proton bursts while systems on the other branch remain comparatively intact.
On the damaged branch Harry Kim dies in a hull breach, Kes crosses a spatial rift, and Wildman's newborn dies; the other branch has living counterparts.
Kes and the intact-branch crew compare phase-shifted biological/ship evidence and establish that another nearly identical Voyager occupies the same spacetime point.
Quantum analysis indicates the divergence field duplicated ordinary matter and biosignatures but not antimatter, leaving both ships drawing from one antimatter source.
The two crews coordinate an attempted ship merge that fails and threatens mutual annihilation as their phase separation increases.
The two Janeways independently reason through sacrifice, with the damaged-ship captain deciding her branch should be destroyed so the intact branch can survive.
Vidiians board the intact/attacked branch; its Janeway initiates self-destruct, destroying that Voyager and the boarding force.
Before self-destruction, living Harry Kim and Wildman's infant cross the rift to the damaged surviving Voyager, replacing no one by identity fiat but joining a crew whose local counterparts died.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A spatial scission creates two co-located Voyager branches sharing one antimatter source, then asymmetric damage and a Vidiian attack force irreversible survival choices.
neutral_coding.identity_epistemics: Duplicated people and ships remain work-local counterparts with shared causal history; surviving Kim and infant are not silently merged with dead counterparts.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: The branches are described as duplicated matter rather than a simple preexisting parallel universe, but philosophical numerical identity is not settled by the mechanism alone.
